note: E-55 (June 2009) describes KODACHROME 25/64/200 as 'natural colors' that reproduce 'subtle color naturally'; photographers rank KODACHROME 25/64 a little above the natural E-6 films (EKTACHROME 64/100, E100S/G, PROVIA 100F) and below VELVIA / E100VS. K-14 forms the dyes in the colour developers, so its interimage effects come from the black-and-white first development (as in E-6) and are not shown by the neutral-exposure curves. One scale for all three stocks: same process and dye set, so the sheet's own ranking (K25 ~ K64 > K200) is kept. Digitisation verified against the PDF.
